body:
# Literature review: Mersenne-weight criterion for target-three norms (finished bounded pass, baseline `ae8a4e7`)

## Conclusion

I found no published theorem among the sources I could read that implies the Mersenne-weight criterion. None of them states its cyclotomic application (that sqrt(C_e²+8) lies in no cyclotomic field) either. **Priority is still undetermined**, because the most relevant older paper is still unread:

- **Rotkiewicz 1983 is still unread.** I tried every legitimate route: the publisher page (it offers a free CC-BY download), the publisher's download link, the ICM archive PDF, the Polish Digital Mathematics Library (PLDML) record, the zbMATH record and EuDML. The download link just redirects to the ICM archive, which returned HTTP 403. PLDML and the zbMATH web page also returned 403, and EuDML failed with an expired certificate. zbMATH's API record for it has no review text. I did not try to get around any of these blocks.
- **The two later papers that quote it disagree, but the disagreement doesn't matter for us.** Luca–Walsh (2001) and Yuan–Li (2009) quote its Theorems 3 and 5 with the Jacobi symbols swapped. Under either version, the theorem about P_p = x² does not cover our parameters. So the square question does not depend on which version is right.
- **The 1986 Patras chapter is irrelevant.** Its zbMATH review shows it is about Jacobi symbols of Fibonacci numbers and Fibonacci pseudoprimes. It covers neither our parameters nor primitive factors.
- **Later citations gave no match.** The closest hit is a 2007 thesis (Juricevic) on Lehmer numbers with at least two primitive divisors. Results of that kind cannot show N_e is not a square.

## Source-by-source comparison

**1. Rotkiewicz, *Applications of Jacobi's symbol to Lehmer's numbers*, Acta Arith. 42 (1983), 163–187.**
DOI 10.4064/aa-42-2-163-187, MR 84m:10010, Zbl 0519.10004. The date is given as 1982 by MathDoc and 1983 by IMPAN, EuDML and the author's own list. zbMATH keywords: Jacobi symbol, Lehmer number, solvability of Diophantine equations, Catalan equation; MSC 11A15, 11B37, 11D41.
- **Inspected:** bibliographic records only ([IMPAN](https://www.impan.pl/en/publishing-house/journals-and-series/acta-arithmetica/all/42/22/103738/applications-of-jacobi-s-symbol-to-lehmer-s-numbers), [MathDoc](https://geodesic.mathdoc.fr/articles/10.4064/aa-42-2-163-187/), [MaRDI](https://portal.mardi4nfdi.de/wiki/Item:Q3669486), [author's list](https://www.impan.pl/~rotkiewi/)), plus the two later quotations.
- **The orientation clash, read from the PDF page images:**
  - Luca–Walsh, p. 48:
    - R1 (= Rotkiewicz Thm 5, about P_p = p·x²): (L,M)≡(1,0) mod 4 with (M/L)=1, or (0,3) mod 4 with (L/M)=1.
    - R2 (= Thm 3, about P_p = x²): (3,0) mod 4 with (M/L)=1, or (0,1) mod 4 with (L/M)=1.
  - Yuan–Li, p. 276: the same congruence cases, with every Jacobi symbol swapped.
- **Our first Lehmer description, (L,M)=(8,−1):** this is (0,3) mod 4.
  - R2 needs (3,0) or (0,1), so it does not apply under either version. **Known: no subsumption of the square question.**
  - R1's case (0,3) does match. The symbol is (8/−1) in one version and (−1/8) in the other; I did not determine whether the original treats either as defined and equal to +1. In any case R1 concerns U_p = p·x², a different equation. **Unresolved, and not used.**
- **A pitfall worth recording.** If (12,1) is used as *first* Lehmer parameters, the roots are λ and λ⁻¹, and λ−λ⁻¹ = 2√2. Then P_p = W_p (1, 11, 109, …), not U_p. (12,1) is ≡ (0,1) mod 4, so quoted R2 would make W_p a non-square. That statement is about W, not U, and must not be cited for N_e. *Derived here algebraically from the definitions.*
- **What the paper is about.** Judging from its title, keywords and these quotations, it studies Jacobi symbols (P_n/P_m) between two terms of the same sequence. Our criterion uses the Legendre symbol modulo a Mersenne prime ℓ, and ℓ is not a term of this sequence. Nothing quoted gives (N_e/ℓ). **Unresolved:** the full text could still contain a theorem about primitive parts or characters.

**2. Rotkiewicz, *Problems on Fibonacci numbers and their generalizations*.**
In *Fibonacci Numbers and Their Applications* (Patras 1984), Math. Appl. 28, Reidel (1986), 241–255. MR 87k:11025, Zbl 0594.10004.
- **Inspected:** the zbMATH review by K. Szymiczek, fetched through api.zbmath.org. The zbmath.org web page returned 403, and I did not find the Springer full text.
- **Content per the review:** it computes (u_n/u_m) for Fibonacci numbers with coprime indices not divisible by 3, via the Euclidean algorithm. It also discusses Fibonacci pseudoprimes, proves an existence theorem for one type, and lists six problems about pseudoprimes.
- **Assessment:** no direct match. This judgement rests on the review, not the full text.

**3. [Luca–Walsh 2001](https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/83508) and [Yuan–Li 2009](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/83333).**
- I re-read pp. 47–48 and pp. 275–277 from the page images. Their main theorems need (2,1) and (2,3) mod 4 respectively. **Known: they don't apply to (0,3).**

**4. Juricevic, *Lehmer Numbers with at Least 2 Primitive Divisors*, PhD thesis, Waterloo (2007).**
[UWSpace](https://uwspace.uwaterloo.ca/bitstreams/dc24ca7f-d2c2-400f-b42d-57719f0e532e/download)
- **Inspected:** abstract, contents and list of tables (pp. iii–viii).
- **Result:** at least two primitive divisors when n/(ηκ) is an odd integer, apart from explicitly tabulated exceptions. κ is a squarefree kernel. For (8,−1), whether odd n with 3 | n qualifies depends on the sign convention for κ, which I did not check.
- **Assessment:** even if it applies, two primitive divisors do not show N_e is not a square. **No direct match.** It is relevant mainly as a sign of Aurifeuillian structure at 3 | e.

**5. Lesser leads, all no direct match.**
- [Prime Pages, "Lehmer primitive part"](https://t5k.org/top20/page.php?id=68): with R = P+2 and Q = 1, our (12,1) gives P = 10. That is the Lucas sequence x_n = U_n·W_n. Its Aurifeuillian split at n = 3^r·m^s is factorization data, not characters.
- Broadhurst's [OEIS A158892](https://oeis.org/A158892): primality indices for this exact λ. Primality only.
- [Roettger–Williams, JIS 28 (2025)](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL28/Roettger/roettger15.html): which starting values work in Lucas–Lehmer-type tests. Mechanism precedent only, as with Gross.

**Claim labels**
- Bumby gives the whole-term and prime-source results: **known**.
- Mersenne-weight criterion: **no direct match among inspected sources; Rotkiewicz 1983 unresolved**.
- Cyclotomic/geometric application: **no direct match among inspected sources**.
- General target-three norm claim: no stronger theorem found, so it **remains unresolved**.
- Finite-difference and Lucas–Lehmer field mechanisms: **known methods**.

## Replacement text for `LITERATURE_REVIEW132.md`

**Replace "## Unresolved leads and the next bounded step" with:**

```markdown
## Remaining leads (bounded pass completed 2026-11-24, baseline ae8a4e7)

1. Rotkiewicz, *Applications of Jacobi's symbol to Lehmer's numbers*,
   Acta Arith. 42 (1983), 163–187, DOI 10.4064/aa-42-2-163-187,
   MR 84m:10010, Zbl 0519.10004. **Full text still not inspected.**
   The IMPAN "free download" link redirects to the ICM archive
   (`matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/aa/aa42/aa4224.pdf`), which returned HTTP 403;
   the PLDML record and the zbMATH web page also returned 403, the EuDML
   record (doc 205870) could not be fetched (expired certificate), and the
   zbMATH API record has no review. Access controls were not bypassed.
   From primary quotations (Luca–Walsh p. 48; Yuan–Li p. 276):
   - The two papers give the same congruence cases for Rotkiewicz's
     Theorems 3 and 5 but swap every Jacobi symbol. The original was not
     read, so the discrepancy is unresolved.
   - It does not affect squares: Theorem 3 (P_p=x^2) needs (L,M) ≡ (3,0)
     or (0,1) mod 4, and our first Lehmer pair (8,-1) is (0,3) in both
     versions.
   - Theorem 5 (P_p=p*x^2) has a (0,3) case, but it is a different
     equation and is not used.
   - Taking (12,1) as *first* Lehmer parameters gives P_p=W_p, not U_p;
     results about that sequence must not be cited for N_e.
   - Its subject, as indicated by title, keywords and quotations, is Jacobi
     symbols between two terms of one sequence. That is not a Legendre
     symbol modulo a Mersenne prime that is not a term. Whether the full
     text contains a primitive-part or character theorem covering our
     criterion remains unchecked.
2. Rotkiewicz, *Problems on Fibonacci numbers and their generalizations*,
   Math. Appl. 28 (1986), 241–255, MR 87k:11025, Zbl 0594.10004. Only the
   zbMATH review (K. Szymiczek) was inspected: Jacobi symbols of Fibonacci
   numbers, Fibonacci pseudoprimes, six open problems. No direct relevance
   was found.
3. Later citations checked: the Juricevic thesis (Waterloo 2007; abstract,
   contents and tables only), Prime Pages "Lehmer primitive part",
   OEIS A158892, and Roettger–Williams (JIS 2025). These concern counts of
   primitive divisors, Aurifeuillian splitting, primality and Lucas–Lehmer
   starting values. None gives quadratic characters of
   Phi_e(lambda,-lambda^-1) modulo Mersenne primes, and two primitive
   divisors would not prove nonsquareness.

No MathSciNet or zbMATH forward-citation search was available. Search-engine
summaries were used only as leads.
```

**Replace the conclusion paragraph (lines 6–11) with:**

```markdown
The established ingredients have identifiable precedents: Bumby (1967)
for whole terms and prime sources, and standard finite-difference and
Lucas–Lehmer finite-field mechanisms. Among the sources inspected, no
theorem states or implies the Mersenne-weight criterion or its
cyclotomic-field application. The main inspected Lehmer square theorems
(Rotkiewicz's Theorem 3 as quoted by both later papers, Luca–Walsh,
Yuan–Li, McDaniel) exclude our parameters by their hypotheses. Priority
remains **undetermined**: the original Rotkiewicz (1983) full text could
not be retrieved, and forward-citation coverage is incomplete. Erdős #132
and the general target-three norm claim remain unresolved.
```

## Bibliography additions

- A. Rotkiewicz, *Problems on Fibonacci numbers and their generalizations*, in A. N. Philippou, G. E. Bergum, A. F. Horadam (eds.), *Fibonacci Numbers and Their Applications*, Math. Appl. 28, Reidel, 1986, 241–255. MR 87k:11025, Zbl 0594.10004. Review only.
- R. Juricevic, *Lehmer Numbers with at Least 2 Primitive Divisors*, PhD thesis, University of Waterloo, 2007. Abstract, contents and tables only.
- E. L. Roettger, H. C. Williams, *Some Remarks Concerning the Lucas–Lehmer Primality Test*, J. Integer Seq. 28 (2025), Art. 25.2.5.
- D. Broadhurst, OEIS [A158892](https://oeis.org/A158892).
- For the existing Rotkiewicz 1983 entry, add MR 84m:10010, Zbl 0519.10004 and the access-failure note.
- In the JSON ledger, set `rotkiewicz1986.inspected` to "zbMATH review (Szymiczek)". Keep `priority_assessment: "undetermined"`.

I edited no files and ran no scripts. The page and theorem details for Luca–Walsh, Yuan–Li and Juricevic come from PDF page images I read myself. Everything else comes from the publisher, zbMATH and author records listed above.
